title: G3: Finiteness of the solution set with an explicit length/diameter bound

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap G3.** 'Enumerate every solution' is only well-posed if the solution set is finite. Must prove $\exists B$ with $x_e\le B$ for every solution, and compute $B$ explicitly.

Suggested mechanism: if some $x_e$ is too large, the direct subdivided path along $e$ between its endpoints $u,v$ ceases to be the geodesic, because a 2-arc detour $u\to w\to v$ through a common neighbour $w$ (of bounded total subdivided length) becomes shorter -- or ties it, breaking uniqueness. Since $H$ has diameter 2, every non-adjacent pair has a common neighbour and every adjacent pair lies on a pentagon, giving competing routes of bounded length. Turn this into an explicit inequality $x_e \le f(\text{other } x)$ and derive a uniform bound $B$. Without G3 the algorithm in G4 has no finite search domain.
